title: A per-host install section in the README, all four hosts
description:
The README must itself tell a reader how to install the SOBER plugin into the agentic tool they use — not link them elsewhere for it. Write one subsection per host under the guide's install step, each with the exact commands and each stating the shared prerequisite once: `sober` has to be on PATH (`npm i -g @besober/cli`) because every host's MCP declaration and Claude Code's hooks.json name that command.

Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add memoksin/sober` then `/plugin install sober@sober` — no checkout, Claude Code clones the repository itself from the root .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; plus the settings.json route (extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins) for a team that wants it present on checkout.
Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add <path to checkout>` then `codex plugin add sober@sober` — a checkout is required, because .agents/plugins/marketplace.json declares source `local` with path ./packages/codex-plugin.
Cursor: symlink packages/cursor-plugin into ~/.cursor/plugins/local/sober, reload, confirm under Customize — checkout required.
OpenCode: copy packages/opencode-plugin/.opencode into the project or ~/.config/opencode/, and merge the mcp block of opencode.json — checkout required.

Each subsection ends with the one line that matters for that host, taken from the Hosts table rather than repeating it: whether decisions can be asked in session, and whether an attended run is possible. Verify every command against the repository before writing it; a command that does not run is worse than a link.

brief.approach:
One file, `README.md`. The placeholder is already in place: line 51 is `<!-- per-host install sections land here: node ykg6 -->`, sitting under the `## Install the plugin for your host` heading whose prose already states the shared prerequisite (`sober` on PATH, because every host's MCP declaration names that command and Claude Code's `hooks.json` names it too). Replace that one comment line with four `###` subsections, in the Hosts-table order: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode. Change nothing else on the page — not the `## Install` section above (the npm install and `sober init` stay where they are), not the Hosts table below, which already says "The install commands for each host are under **Install the plugin for your host** above" and keeps only the four differing columns.

Every command is copied from the host package README it came from, not invented. Verified against the repository today:

- **Claude Code** — no checkout. `/plugin marketplace add memoksin/sober` then `/plugin install sober@sober`; Claude Code clones the repository itself from the root `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, whose one plugin entry has source `./packages/claude-code-plugin`. Then the second, equally true route for a team that wants the plugin present on checkout: `extraKnownMarketplaces` + `enabledPlugins` in `settings.json`. Note that the `packages/claude-code-plugin` README does not exist yet — node `write-the-missing-readme-for-packages-cl-sshg` writes it — so do not link to `packages/claude-code-plugin/README.md` from here; the Hosts table's bare-directory link is the one that is true today and it is not this node's to change.
- **Cursor** — checkout required. `ln -s /path/to/sober/packages/cursor-plugin ~/.cursor/plugins/local/sober`, reload Cursor, confirm the skills and the MCP server under **Customize**. Local plugin imports have to be allowed (`packages/cursor-plugin/README.md:8-19`).
- **Codex** — checkout required. `codex plugin marketplace add /path/to/sober` then `codex plugin add sober@sober`. The path is the repository root, not the package: `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` declares source `local` with path `./packages/codex-plugin` (`packages/codex-plugin/README.md:7-17`).
- **OpenCode** — checkout required, and it is not a marketplace package. `cp -r packages/opencode-plugin/.opencode <your project>/.opencode`, then merge `opencode.json`'s `mcp` block into the project's own; globally, the same two into `~/.config/opencode/` (`packages/opencode-plugin/README.md:8-22`).

Each subsection opens with one line saying whether a checkout is needed — that is the difference a reader is scanning for — and closes with one line taken from the Hosts table rather than restating it: whether decisions can be asked in session, and whether an attended run is possible. Claude Code yes/yes, Cursor yes/no, Codex no/no, OpenCode no/no. Do not repeat the `npm i -g @besober/cli` prerequisite inside each block; the section's opening paragraph already says it once, which is the point of having the section.

Register is the README's own: short sentences, imperative, fenced blocks with no `$` prompt, no marketing. Keep the file's existing tab-free markdown and its ~80-column prose wrap — biome does not format markdown, so the wrap is by hand and a reflowed paragraph is noise in the diff.

acceptance.proves: the four host subsections exist as `###` headings under the install section; the README had no `###` heading at that level before except `### A second machine, Windows included`, so this reads 5
the placeholder comment was replaced, not left sitting above the new prose

acceptance.run: for h in 'Claude Code' Cursor Codex OpenCode; do grep -q "^### $h" README.md || { echo "missing: $h"; exit 1; }; done && echo all four hosts
acceptance.proves: all four supported hosts are covered, each by name, none skipped

acceptance.run: grep -q 'plugin marketplace add memoksin/sober' README.md && grep -q 'codex plugin marketplace add' README.md && grep -q '~/.cursor/plugins/local/sober' README.md && grep -q 'packages/opencode-plugin/.opencode' README.md
acceptance.proves: each host's real install command is on the page, matching the command its own package README gives — a reader can copy it and it runs
only README.md changed: no package README, no code, no test, no CI file was touched
biome and secretlint are clean on the changed file
